title: Tangent lines and radii (right angles, isosceles triangles)
subtitle: Circles · 7 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **7 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 0 Easy, 0 Medium, 7 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see the word 'tangent', or a triangle or quadrilateral with a vertex at the center and other vertices on the circle.
- In the xy-plane version, you are given a center and a point of tangency and asked for the tangent line's slope, or which point lies on the tangent line.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Any two segments from the center to the circle are radii, so they are equal.
- That makes triangles with a vertex at the center isosceles.
- 2) A tangent line meets the radius at a right angle.
- In coordinates, find the slope of the radius and take its negative reciprocal.
- 3) Two tangent segments drawn from the same outside point are equal.
- Use this to split the figure into two congruent right triangles and apply the Pythagorean theorem or area formulas.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: For coordinate versions, plot the center and the point of tangency.
Then type y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) using the negative-reciprocal slope, and check which answer choice lies on that line.
For geometric figures with no coordinates, Desmos only helps with the arithmetic.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You use the slope of the radius itself as the tangent's slope, or you take the reciprocal without changing the sign.
In figures, you miss that the sides from the center are both radii, or that the angle between radius and tangent is 90°.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You use the slope of the radius itself as the tangent's slope, or you take the reciprocal without changing the sign.
In figures, you miss that the sides from the center are both radii, or that the angle between radius and tangent is 90°.
